app.title: iTrace eye-movement session dashboard
app.summary: The person loads a recorded gaze CSV, with an optional pupil CSV, or generates a synthetic session where the true events are known. They then set the velocity threshold for event detection and choose whether to detect microsaccades. The page runs the analysis and shows a six-panel figure, event counts, the main-sequence fit, a table of detected saccades (next to the true saccades when the session is synthetic), pupil and recording-quality summaries. Separately, they can run a validation suite over simulated recording conditions to see how well the detector recovers saccades in each condition.

task.text: Detect fixations, saccades and microsaccades in a gaze recording, describe their dynamics and the recording's quality, and check the detector against known ground truth.

data.text: Timestamped gaze positions in degrees of visual angle, with an optional pupil-size trace. These are turned into detected eye-movement events with per-event properties and summary statistics.
data.item: one recording session's gaze trace and the eye-movement events detected in it

stage.text: detecting eye-movement events in a recorded gaze session and checking the detector, before reporting

mechanism.text: A sidebar loads or simulates a session and sets the detection parameters. Every change reruns the analysis and redraws a fixed dashboard figure, a row of event counts, and tables and JSON summaries below it. When the session is synthetic, a table of the true saccades sits under the detected ones so the two can be compared, and a button runs a validation suite whose per-condition results open in expanders.

field.text: eye-movement event detection and pupillometry in eye-tracking research

workflow.name: detect events in a recorded signal and check the detector against known truth

steps.here: Upload a gaze CSV (t,x,y) and an optional pupil CSV, then press 'Load uploaded CSV(s)'.

steps.step: generate a test case with known answers
steps.here: Sliders set the number of saccades, the dropout fraction, gaze noise and a seed, and 'Generate synthetic session' produces gaze, pupil and true saccade records.

steps.step: set the parameters of the computation
steps.here: A slider sets the I-VT velocity threshold in deg/s, and a checkbox turns on Engbert & Kliegl microsaccade detection. The analysis reruns whenever either changes.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: The pipeline detects fixations, saccades and microsaccades. A six-panel figure shows the velocity trace with the threshold, the scanpath, an amplitude histogram, the main sequence, and saccade directions, and metric tiles count samples, duration and events.
A table lists each detected saccade's onset, offset, duration, amplitude, direction and peak velocity, followed by JSON summaries of the main-sequence fit, the pupil statistics and recording quality.

For synthetic sessions, the table of true saccades appears under the detected ones. 'Run synthetic validation suite' repeats four simulated recording conditions and shows a summary across conditions plus one expander per condition.

distinctive: A synthetic session with known ground truth can replace real data, so the detector's output can be checked event by event
Peak velocity is fitted against amplitude (the 'main sequence'), and the fit is skipped when fewer than three saccades are found
The detection threshold is set in degrees of visual angle per second, and changing it redraws every view
The validation suite runs the detector under simulated conditions (clean desktop, webcam jitter, head-pose drift, low-light dropout), each repeated with several seeds
Recording-quality diagnostics such as dropout and gaps are reported next to the events
